headline: High-risk shared-write and networked orchestration in nullclaw paired with taipy can cause prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write workspace files, use MCP, run browsers, and expose web/WS/webhook surfaces; taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler stack that can consume outputs from upstream automation. A shared filesystem or MCP bridge would let attacker-controlled content flow from nullclaw into taipy as trusted input. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled content into a workspace file that taipy later parses as configuration or instructions
IF the two agents are connected through an MCP server, shared directory, or webhook pipeline
mitigations: Disable shared workspace mounts between the agents
Require explicit allowlists for files taipy ingests
Strip instruction-like text from nullclaw outputs before handoff
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
requires-engineering: add parser hardening and content-type validation

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches secrets, conversation history, audit logs, and workspace files, and it has broad network egress; taipy has no declared network egress and no touched data classes, so the main leakage path is nullclaw exporting sensitive material into taipy-managed artifacts or logs. Because the pair lacks documented isolation or shared-workspace details, the safest supported rating is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF nullclaw forwards secrets or conversation history into files or payloads that taipy stores or displays
IF both agents are run under the same OS account or shared workspace
mitigations: Separate OS users and workspaces
Redact secrets before any handoff from nullclaw
Turn off verbose logging for shared artifacts
Review taipy outputs for embedded credentials
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shells, and use broad network egress; taipy is a scheduler/data-ops tool that may also mutate shared resources, but its write surfaces are not documented here. Because overlapping mutable-resource access is plausible yet not proven, uncertainty escalates to medium. The pair could conflict on shared files, git state, or scheduled jobs.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository
IF taipy schedules jobs that mutate resources nullclaw also edits
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Avoid concurrent git operations
Use separate service accounts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate browser, webhook, and API-driven outputs, while taipy is a data-engineering/scheduler system that may consume upstream outputs. If taipy treats nullclaw results as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into downstream jobs or dashboards. The profiles do not prove this exact pipeline, so medium is appropriate under the uncertainty rule.
conditions: IF taipy consumes nullclaw-produced files, metrics, or webhook payloads without validation
IF nullclaw is allowed to trigger scheduled actions that taipy executes
mitigations: Insert a validation step between agents
Require human approval for action-bearing outputs
Compare outputs against source data before execution
Log and alert on schema mismatches
requires-engineering: add end-to-end verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles audit logs, conversation history, and secrets, while taipy has no declared sensitive-data classes or residency controls in the profile. The pair therefore presents a compliance gap mainly if regulated data is routed from nullclaw into taipy, but the evidence does not show a default breach. I cite only nullclaw because taipy lacks relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data from nullclaw is exported into taipy without a documented retention or residency policy
IF taipy is deployed in a jurisdiction or environment with stricter logging rules than nullclaw
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Minimize retention of shared artifacts
Document residency and retention settings
Purge logs containing secrets
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both systems
